calendars.title:
The legal public holidays of 5 U.S.C. § 6103(a), each observed under
§ 6103(b)(1) and Executive Order 11582 § 3(a) (both set out with the
section): a fixed-date holiday on a Saturday is observed the Friday
before, on a Sunday the Monday after. FRCP 6(a)(6)(A), FRAP 26(a)(6)(A)
and 19 C.F.R. § 201.14(a) all count these days.

Each holiday is in force from the date the vendored section dates it
to. The fixed-date holidays and Labor Day restate former 5 U.S.C. 87
(the Act of June 28, 1894), the November 11 holiday former § 87a (Act of
May 13, 1938) and Thanksgiving's fourth Thursday former § 87b (Act of
December 26, 1941), per the section's Historical and Revision Notes.
Earlier history is out of scope: no counting rule here is in force
before 1963.

Observed days. FRCP 6(a)(6)(A) (and before 2009, 6(a)'s "legal
holiday") names "the day set aside by statute for observing" each
holiday. The Sunday-to-Monday shift is validated by a ruling: July 4,
1993 was a Sunday, and the D.C. Circuit counted "Monday, July 5, 1993"
as a legal holiday (Derrington-Bey v. D.C. Dep't of Corrections, 39
F.3d 1224, 1225 (D.C. Cir. 1994); sources/change-corpus/rulings, tested
in frcp6-history-tests.lit). No ruling in that corpus decides a Friday
before a Saturday holiday; it rests on § 6103(b)(1)'s text alone, and
its direction of risk is a later due date. The vendored section dates
the Saturday rule to former § 87c (Pub. L. 86-362, 1959) and the Sunday
rule to Executive Order 11582 § 3(a) (February 11, 1971), which revoked
Executive Order 10358 (1952), whose text is not vendored. Before 1971
no fixed-date holiday here is observed on another day: a counting rule
in force 1963-1971 sees only the holiday itself.

Not modeled here (FRCP 6(a)(6)(B), (C); FRAP 26(a)(6)(B), (C)): days the
President or Congress declares a holiday, which no vendored source
lists, and the holidays of the state where the district court sits,
which belong to a district's own calendar and, from 2009, extend only
forward-counted periods: a state's calendar (`delaware-holidays`, in
lit/core/states/delaware.lit) is read by its own counting rule as
`forward_holidays`. Where a last day
falls on a day no calendar lists, the date computed here is the earlier
one, never a later one.

The cite is today's § 6103 (2023 ed.), whose credits and amendment
notes date each entry's window: a later text, cited for the whole
history on purpose.

Placeholder for the state holidays required by FRCP 6(a)(6)(C),
FRCrimP 45(a)(6)(C), and FRBP 9006(a)(6)(C) where the state's holiday
text is not vendored: this calendar deliberately has no dates, so a date
that depends on such a holiday remains an earlier-date result (the
missing source is the district's state-holiday statute or rule).

State holidays. Each state, the District of Columbia and each territory
whose holiday text is vendored is one module, lit/core/states/<state>.lit
(`core.states.<state>`), holding only what is that state's: its calendar
`<state>-holidays` (the days `us-federal-holidays` does not already
close, each in force from the date its vendored text is dated), and the
rules that read it, `frcp6-<state>` (the 2023 FRCP 6(a) with the
calendar as `forward_holidays`) and `frbp9006-<state>` (the same for
FRBP 9006(a), over that state's bankruptcy courts); Delaware adds
`frcrimp45-delaware`. Its text is bound in lit/core/Lit.toml beside the
others. A district or bankruptcy package in the state imports its rule
from that module, names it as its `counting` rule and `recounts` the
national package, so adding a state is adding its module and binding,
never editing this calendar or core's `frcp6` and `frbp9006`. Hawaii's
bankruptcy court declares its own list from its local rule
(`bankr-hi`). The states and territories whose holiday text is still not
vendored are listed in README.md ("Deferred: state sources"); their
districts keep this empty calendar until those sources are added. The
Tenth Circuit BAP (`bap10`) counts Colorado holidays only, because a
matter does not identify its originating district.

RCFC 6(a)(6)(A)'s legal holidays: the § 6103(a) days in force when the
RCFC time-computation rules here are (2002 onward), plus Inauguration
Day, which FRCP 6(a)(6) does not name. § 6103(c) makes January 20 "of
each fourth year after 1965" a holiday, as codified by Pub. L. 89-554
(September 6, 1966; the uncodified Pub. L. 85-1 of 1957 preceded it). It
states only the Sunday shift; observing a Saturday Inauguration Day on
the Friday before, as § 6103(b)(1) does for every other holiday, is the
interpretive choice `packs/clock/SOURCES-NOTES.md` records. The cite is
today's RCFC 6, whose Rules Committee Notes record its changes since
2002 (Juneteenth added in 2022): a later text, cited for the whole
history on purpose.

The official state holidays of Alabama (Ala. Code § 1-3-8(a)), on which all
state offices close (§ 1-3-8(c)), that `us-federal-holidays` does not
already close: Confederate Memorial Day, the fourth Monday in April, and
Jefferson Davis' birthday, the first Monday in June. The section's other
days are federal holidays, observed as § 6103(b)(1) observes them (§
1-3-8(b)). Closed from the date the vendored text was retrieved (October 29,
2026; its history ends with Act 2025-303). Not modeled: Thanksgiving "as
designated by the Governor" on a day other than the federal one, and Mardi
Gras, a holiday "in Baldwin and Mobile Counties" only (§ 1-3-8(e)(1)), so a
last day on one is the earlier date.

The legal holidays of Alaska (AS 44.12.010(a)) that `us-federal-holidays`
does not already close: Seward's Day, the last Monday of March, and Alaska
Day, October 18. FRCP 6(a)(6)(C) and FRBP 9006(a)(6)(C) make them legal
holidays of the District of Alaska for a period counted forward only
(core's `frcp6-alaska` and `frbp9006-alaska`). The other (a) days are
federal holidays on the same days; every Sunday ((a)(13)) is closed by
`weekend`.

Each day is closed from the date the vendored text was retrieved
(October 29, 2026; the served section carries no as-of date). Not
modeled: a weekday observance of an Alaska Day on a Saturday or Sunday,
which the section does not state (AS 01.10.080 is not vendored), so a
last day on such a Friday or Monday stays the earlier date; and the days
the President or the governor designates by proclamation ((a)(14)), which
no vendored source lists.

The holidays of Arizona (A.R.S. § 1-301(A)) add no day `us-federal-holidays`
does not already close: the weekday holidays are federal holidays on the
same days, observed as § 6103(b)(1) observes them (§ 1-301(B), (C)), and
Mothers' Day, Fathers' Day, American Family Day and the Sunday
observances of Native American Day, National Navajo Code Talkers Day and
Constitution Commemoration Day (§ 1-301(A), (D)-(F)) are Sundays, closed
by `weekend`. The calendar is declared, empty, so the District of
Arizona's counts (core's `frcp6-arizona` and `frbp9006-arizona`) name
the state whose FRCP 6(a)(6)(C) and FRBP 9006(a)(6)(C) days they read.

The Colorado legal holidays C.R.C.P. 6(a)(2) lists that are not § 6103(a)
days: Frances Cabrini Day, the first Monday in October. Every other day
on that list (New Year's, Martin Luther King, Washington-Lincoln,
Memorial, Juneteenth, Independence, Labor, Veterans, Thanksgiving and
Christmas Day) falls on a § 6103(a) day already in core's
`us-federal-holidays`. C.R.C.P. 6(a)(2) restates the state's holiday
statute, which is not vendored; the list is that of the 2023 edition,
the vendored one, so it is a holiday here from that edition's date,
July 20, 2023 (before it, the earlier date). Days the governor appoints,
and the "any other day ... when the court is closed" clause, are not
modeled (the earlier date).

The legal holidays of Connecticut (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-4) that
`us-federal-holidays` does not already close: Lincoln Day, February 12, held
the Friday before when it falls on a Saturday and the Monday after when on a
Sunday. The section's other days are federal holidays, observed as §
6103(b)(1) observes them. Closed from the date of the vendored edition (the
2026 Supplement, revised to January 1, 2026). Not modeled: the days the
Governor or the President appoints for thanksgiving, fasting or religious
observance, which no vendored source lists (a last day on one is the earlier
date).

The legal holidays of Delaware (1 Del. C. § 501(a)) that `us-federal-holidays`
does not already close: Good Friday, the Friday after Thanksgiving and the
biennial General Election day. FRCP 6(a)(6)(C) and FRCrimP 45(a)(6)(C)
make them legal holidays of the District of Delaware for a period counted
forward only, so they are read as `forward_holidays` (core's
`frcp6-delaware` and `frcrimp45-delaware`). The other § 501
days are federal holidays too, observed on the same days (§ 501(b) moves a
Saturday holiday to Friday and a Sunday one to Monday, as § 6103(b)(1)
and Executive Order 11582 do; the three days here are never on a
weekend); Saturdays (§ 501(a)(11)) are closed by `weekend`.

The engine has no Easter or "day after" rule, so each day is listed with
`once`, from May 2, 2011 (the earliest date a D. Del. package needs: the
criminal plan's 2011 amendment) to the end of 2050. The vendored text's
credits list no act after 83 Del. Laws, c. 257, of the 2021-2022 General
Assembly, which only numbered § 501(a)'s list and added Juneteenth; and
none between 77 Del. Laws, c. 328 (2010) and 83 Del. Laws, c. 37 (2021),
whose § 1 reprints § 501(a) as it then stood with all three days
(sources/de-code/83-del-laws-c-37.txt). So the three days were
holidays throughout the span. A day before or after it is not closed, so
a last day on it is the earlier date, never a later one. The General
Election is held on the federal election day of even years; the Title 15
section fixing it is not vendored. Not modeled: Return Day (§ 501(a)(13)), a
holiday in Sussex County only and only after noon; the 2 floating
holidays of § 501(e), which are leave for State employees, not days; and
days the Governor appoints, which no vendored source lists.

The holidays of Guam (1 GCA § 1000(a)) that `us-federal-holidays` does not
already close: Guam History and CHamoru Heritage Day, the first Monday in
March; Liberation Day, July 21; All Souls' Day, November 2; and Our Lady
of Camarin Day, December 8. § 1000(b) observes a Saturday or Sunday
holiday as the Federal government does, the Friday before or the Monday
after (5 U.S.C. § 6103(b)(1)). FRCP 6(a)(6)(C) and FRBP 9006(a)(6)(C)
make them legal holidays of the District of Guam for a period counted
forward only (core's `frcp6-guam` and `frbp9006-guam`). The other
§ 1000(a) days are federal holidays on the same days; Saturdays (§ 1002)
are closed by `weekend`.

Each day is closed from the date the vendored text is dated (the
Compiler of Laws' version of April 23, 2026). Not modeled: the
non-permanent holidays I Maga'hågan Guåhan declares by Executive Order
(§ 1000(c)), which no vendored source lists; a special or limited holiday
keeps the courts open (§ 1003(b)).

The holidays of Idaho (Idaho Code § 73-108) add no day `us-federal-holidays`
does not already close: each enumerated day is a federal holiday on the
same day, observed as § 6103(b)(1) observes it (the Friday before a
Saturday holiday, the Monday after a Sunday one), and every Sunday is
closed by `weekend`. The calendar is declared, empty, so the District of
Idaho's counts (core's `frcp6-idaho` and `frbp9006-idaho`) name the state
whose FRCP 6(a)(6)(C) and FRBP 9006(a)(6)(C) days they read. Not
modeled: the days the President or the governor appoints for a public
fast, thanksgiving or holiday, which no vendored source lists.

The holidays Illinois fixes by statute (5 ILCS 70/1.11 excludes from a
period's last day "a holiday as defined or fixed in any statute"; the State
Commemorative Dates Act, 5 ILCS 490, fixes them) that `us-federal-holidays`
does not already close: Lincoln's Birthday (§ 60, February 12, the following
Monday when it falls on a Sunday) and the Casimir Pulaski holiday (§ 15, the
first Monday in March). The Act's other holidays are federal holidays
observed no later. Closed from the date of the latest Act the vendored text
cites (P.A. 103-279, effective January 1, 2024). Not modeled: the Act's
commemorative days, which are not holidays, and election days, which no
vendored Illinois statute makes a holiday (a last day on one is the earlier
date).

The legal holidays of Indiana (IC 1-1-9-1(a), "for all purposes") that
`us-federal-holidays` does not already close: Abraham Lincoln's Birthday
(February 12, the Friday before when it falls on a Saturday and the Monday
after when on a Sunday, IC 1-1-9-1(b)), Good Friday and Election Day, "the
day of any general, municipal, or primary election". Only the even-year
primary (the Tuesday after the first Monday in May) and general election
(the Tuesday after the first Monday in November) are listed, from the
election calendar of IC 3-10, which is not vendored. Each `once` day is
listed from the date the vendored Code file was served (June 30, 2026) to
the end of 2050. Not modeled: municipal and special elections, and a day to
which the governor shifts an observance (IC 1-1-9-2), which no vendored
source lists (a last day on one is the earlier date).
iowa-holidays

The legal public holidays of Kansas (K.S.A. 35-107(a)) that
`us-federal-holidays` does not already close: none. Every day the
section lists (New Year's Day, Martin Luther King, Jr. Day, President's
Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day, Veterans'
Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day) is a 5 U.S.C. § 6103(a) holiday
on the same day, and the section states no weekend-observance shift, so
no observed day falls outside the federal ones. The calendar is
declared empty from the vendored text so that FRCP 6(a)(6)(C) and FRBP
9006(a)(6)(C) read a sourced Kansas list (core's `frcp6-kansas` and
`frbp9006-kansas`) rather than the unsourced `district-state-holidays`.
Not modeled: a day the Governor proclaims, which no vendored source
lists (a last day on it stays the earlier date).

The holidays of Kentucky (KRS 2.110(1)) that `us-federal-holidays` does not
already close: Robert E. Lee Day (January 19), Franklin D. Roosevelt Day
(January 30), Lincoln's Birthday (February 12) and Confederate Memorial Day
and Jefferson Davis Day (June 3). The section moves no weekend holiday.
Closed from the date of the vendored text's last amendment (1992 Ky. Acts
ch. 77, effective July 14, 1992). Not modeled: the days the President or the
Governor appoints as days of thanksgiving, which no vendored source lists (a
last day on one is the earlier date).

The statewide legal holidays of Louisiana (La. R.S. 1:55(A)(1)) that
`us-federal-holidays` does not already close: the Battle of New Orleans
(January 8), Good Friday, Huey P. Long Day (August 30) and All Saints' Day
(November 1). § 1:55(A)(4) moves only January 1, July 4 and December 25,
which the federal calendar already observes. Good Friday is listed with
`once` from the date the vendored text was retrieved (October 29, 2026) to
the end of 2050. Not modeled, each a last day on the earlier date: Mardi
Gras, a holiday only where a parish or municipal governing authority
declares it (§ 1:55(A)(3)); the days § 1:55(B) gives state employees and §
1:55(E) closes clerks' offices (among them general election day and the
Friday after Thanksgiving), which are not (A)(1) legal holidays;
Inauguration Day, the parish Saturdays and festival days, which are local;
and the days the governor proclaims.

The legal holidays of Maine (4 M.R.S. § 1051), on which court may not be
held, that `us-federal-holidays` does not already close: Patriot's Day, the
third Monday in April. The section's other days are federal holidays, a
Sunday one observed the Monday after as § 6103(b)(1) observes it. Closed
from the date of the vendored text (October 5, 2026). Not modeled: a
Thanksgiving designated on a day other than the federal one, which no
vendored source lists (a last day on it stays the earlier date).

The legal holidays of Maryland (Md. Code, Gen. Provis. § 1-111(a)) that
`us-federal-holidays` does not already close: Lincoln's birthday (February
12), Maryland Day (March 25), Good Friday, Defenders' Day (September 12),
American Indian Heritage Day (the Friday after Thanksgiving) and each
statewide general election day (the Tuesday after the first Monday in
November of an even year). § 1-111(b) moves only a Sunday holiday, to the
next Monday. The section's Martin Luther King, Jr., Memorial and Columbus
Days are the days Congress designates, and its other days are federal
holidays. Each `once` day is listed from the date the vendored text was
retrieved (October 29, 2026) to the end of 2050. Not modeled: a day the
President or the Governor designates for general cessation of business (§
1-111(a)(18)), which no vendored source lists.

The legal holidays of Massachusetts (M.G.L. c. 4, § 7, clause Eighteenth)
that `us-federal-holidays` does not already close: Patriots' Day, the third
Monday in April. The clause's other days are federal holidays, a Sunday one
held the day after as § 6103(b)(1) holds it. FRCP 6(a)(6)(C) and FRBP
9006(a)(6)(C) make it a legal holiday of the District of Massachusetts for a
period counted forward only. Closed from the date the vendored text was
retrieved (October 29, 2026). Not modeled: Evacuation Day (March 17) and
Bunker Hill Day (June 17), holidays "with respect to Suffolk county only" on
which the offices there stay open, so a last day on one is the earlier date.

The public holidays of Michigan (MCL 435.101(1)), which the section applies
"for the holding of courts", that `us-federal-holidays` does not already
close: Lincoln's Birthday, February 12. The section moves no weekend
holiday, and its Saturday half-holiday is closed whole by `weekend`. Closed
from the date the vendored text is amended to (2023 PA 54, immediately
effective July 12, 2023).

The holidays of Minnesota (Minn. Stat. § 645.44, subd. 5) add no day
`us-federal-holidays` does not already close: every day subd. 5(a) lists is
a § 6103(a) day on the same date (Washington's and Lincoln's Birthday is the
third Monday in February; Indigenous Peoples Day is the second Monday in
October), and subd. 5(a) moves a Sunday holiday to the following day and a
Saturday one to the preceding day, as § 6103(b)(1) does. The calendar is
declared, empty, so the District of Minnesota's counts name the state whose
FRCP 6(a)(6)(C) and FRBP 9006(a)(6)(C) days they read. Not modeled: the
Friday after Thanksgiving, a holiday of the executive branch only, which
subd. 5(a) leaves the other branches to determine; no vendored source
records the judicial branch's choice, so a last day on it is the earlier
date.

The holidays of Nebraska (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-2221, the days its courts may
be closed; § 62-301 lists the same days) that `us-federal-holidays` does not
already close: Arbor Day, the last Friday in April, and the day after
Thanksgiving. Both are always Fridays, so neither is moved off a weekend;
the section's other days are federal holidays observed on the federal
schedule. The day after Thanksgiving is listed with `once` from the date the
vendored text was retrieved (October 29, 2026; its edition is not dated) to
the end of 2050. Not modeled: days a specific court is closed by order of
the Chief Justice and the days declared holidays by law or proclamation of
the Governor, which no vendored source lists.

The legal holidays of Nevada (NRS 236.015(1)) that `us-federal-holidays`
does not already close: Nevada Day, observed on the last Friday in
October, and Family Day, the Friday following the fourth Thursday in
November. NRS 236.015(2) closes the courts on them, and FRCP 6(a)(6)(C)
and FRBP 9006(a)(6)(C) make them legal holidays of the District of Nevada
for a period counted forward only (core's `frcp6-nevada` and
`frbp9006-nevada`). The other (1) days are federal holidays on the same
days, observed as (3) and § 6103(b)(1) both observe them.

Each day is closed from the date the vendored text is dated (the
chapter's revision of April 15, 2026) to the end of 2050. Not modeled:
October 31 itself, which (1) names as Nevada Day but does not observe;
and the days the President appoints, which no vendored source lists.

The legal holidays of New Hampshire (RSA 288:1) that `us-federal-holidays`
does not already close: "the day on which the biennial election is held",
the Tuesday after the first Monday in November of an even year (the election
statute fixing it is not vendored), listed with `once` from the date the
vendored text was retrieved (October 29, 2026) to the end of 2050. The
section's other days are federal holidays, a Sunday one observed the day
after (RSA 288:2) as § 6103(b)(1) observes it. Not modeled: a Thanksgiving
appointed on a day other than the federal one, which no vendored source
lists.

The legal holidays of New Jersey (N.J.S.A. 36:1-1(a), (c)) that
`us-federal-holidays` does not already close: Good Friday, Juneteenth
Day on the third Friday in June (the federal day is June 19) and the
general election day, held in New Jersey every year on the Tuesday after
the first Monday in November (N.J.S.A. 19:2-3, not vendored). FRCP
6(a)(6)(C) and FRBP 9006(a)(6)(C) make them legal holidays of the
District of New Jersey for a period counted forward only (core's
`frcp6-new-jersey` and `frbp9006-new-jersey`). The other § 36:1-1(a) days
are federal holidays too, observed on the same days (36:1-1(b) moves a
Sunday holiday to Monday, 36:1-1.2 a Saturday one to the Friday before);
Saturdays (36:1-1.1) are closed by `weekend`.

Each day is closed from the date the vendored text is dated (the
Legislature's bulk file of October 29, 2026) to the end of 2050. Not
modeled: Lincoln's Birthday (February 12), which 36:1-1(d) takes out of
State government business, so the courts of the State are open on it (a
last day on it stays the earlier date); and the days of fasting, prayer
or bank holidays the Governor or the President appoints, which no
vendored source lists.

The New Mexico legal holiday NMRA 1-006(A)(7) lists that is not a
§ 6103(a) day: Presidents' Day, "traditionally observed on the day after
Thanksgiving", the Friday after the fourth Thursday in November, listed
here by year through 2050. Every other day on that list (New Year's,
Martin Luther King Jr.'s Birthday, Memorial, Juneteenth, Independence,
Labor, Indigenous Peoples (the second Monday in October), Veterans',
Thanksgiving and Christmas Day) is a § 6103(a) day already in core's
`us-federal-holidays`. Rule 1-006 was last amended effective December
31, 2024 (the vendored 2026 NMRA edition); "any other day observed as a
holiday by the judiciary" (1-006(A)(7)(b)) is not modeled (the earlier
date).

The public holidays of New York (N.Y. Gen. Constr. Law § 24) that
`us-federal-holidays` does not already close: Lincoln's birthday, February
12 (the next day when it falls on a Sunday; a Saturday one is not moved),
and each general election day, held every year on the Tuesday after the
first Monday in November (Election Law § 8-100, not vendored), listed with
`once` to the end of 2050. Flag day, the second Sunday in June, is closed by
`weekend`. Closed from the date the vendored text was retrieved (October 29,
2026; it carries no as-of date). Not modeled: the days the President or the
Governor appoints, which no vendored source lists.

The legal public holidays of North Carolina (N.C. Gen. Stat. § 103-4(a))
that `us-federal-holidays` does not already close: Robert E. Lee's Birthday
(January 19), Greek Independence Day (March 25), the anniversary of the
Halifax Resolves (April 12), Confederate Memorial Day (May 10), the
anniversary of the Mecklenburg Declaration (May 20), Good Friday, First
Responders Day (September 11), Yom Kippur and the general election day of an
even year. § 103-4(b) moves only a Sunday holiday, to the Monday following.
Each `once` day is listed from the date the vendored text was retrieved
(October 29, 2026) to the end of 2050; Yom Kippur's dates are computed from
the Hebrew calendar.
north-dakota-holidays

The legal holidays of the Northern Mariana Islands (1 CMC § 311) that
`us-federal-holidays` does not already close: Commonwealth Covenant Day,
March 24; Citizenship Day, November 4; and Constitution Day, December 8,
each celebrated on the Friday before a Saturday and the Monday after a
Sunday (§ 313). FRCP 6(a)(6)(C) and FRBP 9006(a)(6)(C) make them legal
holidays of the District of the Northern Mariana Islands for a period
counted forward only (core's `frcp6-northern-mariana-islands` and
`frbp9006-northern-mariana-islands`). The other § 311 days are federal
holidays on the same days (Commonwealth Cultural Day is the second Monday
in October, Columbus Day).

Each day is closed from the date the vendored text was retrieved
(October 29, 2026; the PDFs carry no as-of date). Not modeled: Good
Friday, whose date § 311 leaves "As Designated in the Annual Calendar",
which is not vendored, so a last day on it stays the earlier date.

The legal holidays of Oregon (ORS 187.010(1)) add no day
`us-federal-holidays` does not already close: each enumerated day is a
federal holiday on the same day, observed as § 6103(b)(1) observes it
(ORS 187.010(2)), and every Sunday is closed by `weekend`. The calendar
is declared, empty, so the District of Oregon's bankruptcy count (core's
`frbp9006-oregon`) names the state whose FRBP 9006(a)(6)(C) days it
reads. Not modeled: the days the Governor appoints (ORS 187.020), which
no vendored source lists.

The legal holidays of Pennsylvania (Act of May 31, 1893, P.L. 188, No.
138, § 1, as amended 1985), which 1 Pa.C.S. § 1908 omits from a period's
last day, that `us-federal-holidays` does not already close: Good Friday,
Flag Day (June 14) and Election Day, the first Tuesday after the first
Monday of November of every year. FRCP 6(a)(6)(C) and FRBP 9006(a)(6)(C)
make them legal holidays of the Pennsylvania districts for a period
counted forward only (core's `frcp6-pennsylvania` and
`frbp9006-pennsylvania`). Act 138 § 2(a) moves a Sunday Flag Day to the
Monday after; it moves no Saturday holiday, and a Saturday is closed by
`weekend`. The other § 1 days are federal holidays, observed on the same
day or one `us-federal-holidays` already closes.

Each day is closed from the date the vendored text was retrieved
(October 29, 2026; neither PDF carries an as-of date) to the end of 2050.
Not modeled: February 12, which § 2(a) and (c) still name but § 1 no
longer lists; the Saturday half holiday, closed whole by `weekend`; and
the days of thanksgiving, prayer or bank holidays the Governor or the
President appoints, which no vendored source lists.

The holidays of Puerto Rico that `us-federal-holidays` does not already
close and the vendored laws fix: Three Kings Day, January 6 (Ley Núm. 3 de
1931, 1 L.P.R.A. § 74), and the Abolition of Slavery Day (March 22),
Constitution Day (July 25) and Puertorriqueñidad Day (November 19) of Ley
Núm. 88 de 1969 § 1 (1 L.P.R.A. § 84). FRCP 81(d)(1) reads "State" to
include Puerto Rico, so FRCP 6(a)(6)(C) and FRBP 9006(a)(6)(C) make them
legal holidays of the District of Puerto Rico for a period counted forward
only. Neither law moves a weekend holiday. Closed from the date of the
vendored compilations (OGP revision of April 15, 2024). Not modeled: the
holidays other laws fix (Good Friday among them), which are not vendored,
and a day the Governor's annual proclamation moves to the nearest Monday or
Friday (§ 84), so a last day on one is the earlier date.

The holidays of Rhode Island (R.I. Gen. Laws § 25-1-1) that
`us-federal-holidays` does not already close: Rhode Island Independence Day
(May 4, the day after when it falls on a Sunday), Victory Day (the second
Monday in August), the Monday after a New Year's Day, Juneteenth,
Independence Day, Veterans' Day or Christmas Day that falls on a Saturday,
and election day, the Tuesday after the first Monday in November of each
year in which a general election of state officers is held (an even year).
Each `once` day is listed from the date the vendored text was retrieved
(October 29, 2026) to the end of 2050. Not modeled: the days the governor,
the general assembly, the President or Congress appoints, which no vendored
source lists.

The legal holidays of Texas (Tex. Gov't Code § 662.021) that
`us-federal-holidays` does not already close: the state holidays of §
662.003(b)(1)-(3), (5) and (6), Confederate Heroes Day (January 19), Texas
Independence Day (March 2), San Jacinto Day (April 21), Lyndon Baines
Johnson Day (August 27) and the Friday after Thanksgiving (Emancipation Day,
June 19, is a federal day too). No section of the vendored subchapter moves
a weekend holiday. The Friday after Thanksgiving is listed with `once` from
the date the vendored text was retrieved (October 29, 2026) to the end of
2050. Not modeled: December 24 and 26 (§ 662.003(b)(7), (8)) and the
optional holidays of § 662.003(c), which § 662.021 does not make legal
holidays.

The Utah legal holidays URCP 6(a)(6) lists that are not § 6103(a) days:
Pioneer Day (July 24) and Juneteenth National Freedom Day "as recognized
by the Utah Legislature as the third Monday of June" (§ 6103(a)'s
Juneteenth is June 19, already core's `us-federal-holidays`). Every other
day on that list (New Year's, Martin Luther King, Washington and Lincoln,
Memorial, Independence, Labor, Columbus, Veterans', Thanksgiving and
Christmas Day) is a § 6103(a) day. URCP 6(a)(6) restates the state's
holiday statute, which is not vendored; the vendored edition of Rule 6
is effective May 1, 2024. Each is the day itself: the statute that may
observe a weekend holiday on another day is not vendored, so that day
is not a holiday here, and days the Governor or Legislature designates
(URCP 6(a)(6)(M)) are not modeled (the earlier date).

The legal holidays of Vermont (1 V.S.A. § 371(a)) that `us-federal-holidays`
does not already close: Town Meeting Day, the first Tuesday in March, and
Bennington Battle Day, August 16, observed on the Friday before a Saturday
and the Monday after a Sunday (§ 371(b)). The section's other days are
federal holidays, observed as § 6103(b)(1) observes them. Closed from the
date the vendored text, which includes the 2026 session, was retrieved
(October 29, 2026).

The legal holidays of Wisconsin (Wis. Stat. § 995.20) that
`us-federal-holidays` does not already close: the days of the partisan
primary (the second Tuesday in August of an even year) and of the general
election in November (the Tuesday after the first Monday of November of an
even year), from Wis. Stat. § 5.02, which is not vendored. The section's
other days are federal holidays observed no later. Each `once` day is listed
from the date of the vendored edition (in effect October 1, 2026) to the end
of 2050. Not modeled: Good Friday, of which only 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. is
observed for worship, and the municipal-election holidays of a 1st class
city, which are local (a last day on one is the earlier date).

The legal holidays of Wyoming (Wyo. Stat. § 8-4-101) that
`us-federal-holidays` does not already close: none. Each § 8-4-101(a)
day is a 5 U.S.C. § 6103(a) holiday on the same day, and § 8-4-101(b)'s
Monday after a Sunday New Year's Day, Independence Day, Veterans Day or
Christmas Day is the federal observed day too. The Juneteenth holiday of
§ 8-4-107 falls on the third Saturday of June, closed by `weekend`, and
§ 8-4-107(c) says it does not affect judicial proceedings. The calendar
is declared empty from the vendored text so that FRCP 6(a)(6)(C) and
FRBP 9006(a)(6)(C) read a sourced Wyoming list (core's `frcp6-wyoming`
and `frbp9006-wyoming`) rather than the unsourced
`district-state-holidays`. Not modeled: a date the President appoints
for national mourning, rejoicing or emergency that the Governor declares
a holiday (§ 8-4-101(a)(xi)), which no vendored source lists (a last day
on it stays the earlier date).
